title: Multiplying Decimals: Tenths by Tenths Worksheets
intro: Use an area model to explain why tenths times tenths gives hundredths.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Shade tenths in each direction on a unit square. Count the overlapping hundredths, then connect the model to the written product.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Build the idea with a hundredths square. Divide one whole square into ten equal columns and ten equal rows. Six columns span six tenths of the width. Four rows span four tenths of the height.

The overlapping rectangle covers 4 rows × 6 cells = 24 cells. Each cell is one hundredth of the whole square. Therefore 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.24. The other cells are unshaded; the square still represents one whole.

Ask your student

How many equal small squares make one whole?

If your student needs help

If the decimal point is misplaced, compare the answer with the shaded portion of the square.
